key_insight: PsychFound is a psychiatry-specialized LLM trained on expert knowledge and clinical records that achieves clinical‑grade performance and measurably improves diagnostic and treatment decisions when integrated into clinician workflows.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between general-purpose LLMs and safe, reliable psychiatric decision support by providing a domain-adapted model validated on clinical tasks and deployed with clinician-in-the-loop safeguards.
method: Assembled a psychiatry-focused corpus combining expert guidelines, annotated clinical records, and domain literature for targeted pretraining/fine-tuning.
Applied instruction tuning and alignment with clinician feedback and safety constraints to produce a model tuned for diagnostic and treatment reasoning.
Validated performance on clinical benchmarks and prospective workflow evaluations, measuring diagnostic accuracy, treatment recommendation quality, and clinician acceptance.
impact: Shows that specialty LLMs, when trained and validated with domain data and clinician oversight, can provide clinically useful decision support. AI/ML practitioners can adopt its data curation, alignment, and evaluation pipeline as a template for building responsible healthcare models.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: data sources (guidelines, notes, literature) → training pipeline (pretrain → fine-tune → alignment) → PsychFound model
Performance bar chart: PsychFound vs. general LLMs on diagnostic accuracy and treatment recommendation metrics
Workflow infographic: clinician + PsychFound interaction loop, highlighting points of decision support and safety checks
Safety & validation dashboard: calibration, false-positive/negative rates, and clinician acceptance metrics
paper_title: A domain-adapted large language model to support clinicians in psychiatric clinical practice
paper_authors: Ruoxi Wang, Shuyu Liu, Ling Zhang, Xuequan Zhu, Zhi Yang
